title.value: How Reasonable are Common-Sense Reasoning Tasks: A Case-Study on the Winograd Schema Challenge and SWAG
title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the top of the paper, clearly indicating the paper's focus on examining common-sense reasoning tasks using two benchmarks, the Winograd Schema Challenge and SWAG.
title.quote: How Reasonable are Common-Sense Reasoning Tasks: A Case-Study on the Winograd Schema Challenge and SWAG

analysis.description: This paper investigates the validity of common-sense reasoning task setups, particularly focusing on the Winograd Schema Challenge (WSC) and SWAG. It questions whether recent improvements in these benchmarks truly reflect advancements in common-sense reasoning. The paper proposes new evaluation protocols to ensure rigorous testing of models' capabilities in these tasks.

type.justification: The paper involves experimental protocols and performance evaluations of models on specific tasks, providing empirical evidence regarding the validity of common-sense reasoning tasks.
type.quote: We test several recently proposed systems using our proposed protocols.

name.justification: The paper's main focus is on understanding and improving common-sense reasoning in language models, which falls under the domain of Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: Recent studies have significantly improved the state-of-the-art on common-sense reasoning (CSR) benchmarks like the Winograd Schema Challenge (WSC) and SWAG. The question we ask in this paper is whether improved performance on these benchmarks represents genuine progress towards common-sense-enabled systems.

name.justification: The paper specifically tackles common-sense reasoning benchmarks and evaluates the validity of models claiming to solve such tasks.
name.quote: The progress of these technologies and the general societal reaction toward them greatly depend on advances in CSR, since systems can seem glar- ingly unintelligent when they lack common sense.

name.justification: The paper evaluates machine learning models, including language models and knowledge-based models, for their ability to perform common-sense reasoning.
name.quote: Recently, a number of systems have attained new state-of-the-art results on WSC and SWAG by querying a language model trained on a very large corpus.
